scope: Read-only reconstruction of three mistaken HF runner invocations, their process observations, persisted partial output, and concurrent P2 state. No rerun or device command.
cause: The host validation helper called each saved execution command verbatim. Those command arrays do not include --validate-only. The runner source returns safely at line 67 only when that flag is present; without it, execution continues to the torch/transformers/reference load path at lines 72 onward.

observed.terminated_by: agent SIGTERM to timeout and child after noticing prolonged CPU/RSS; exact wall timestamp not preserved
observed.stdout_stderr: Captured by wrapper pipes and not persisted; no completed return/output was emitted.

attempts.outer_behavior: Unbuffered Python wrapper iterated commands.json groups and used subprocess.run(argv, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE) without appending --validate-only; it printed "validating 1" before waiting.

start_time_observations.discrepancy: The two start-time observations differ by about69 seconds; the timebase discrepancy is unknown. Preserve both; neither is selected as the exact start.

observed.duration_note: Do not report a single exact duration. Root captured a 527.693-second lower bound from /proc stat+btime; the independent ps lstart observation conflicts, so exact duration remains unresolved.

attempts.outcome: The process was observed running the group1 command without --validate-only at high CPU/RSS. persisted_partial_artifact.interpretation: Partial result artifact; retain unchanged as incident evidence, do not use as a completed control or score.
persisted_partial_artifact.attribution: The report mtime falls within the combined A/B incident interval. Because A and B used the same group1 output path and no pre-attempt file hash was captured, do not attribute this partial artifact to one specific attempt.

p2_overlap.overlap: P2 was already running before the first runner attempt and remained running at the root stop observation. Attempt B overlaps P2; exact runner start and duration are unresolved due conflicting process timebases. Attempts A/C absolute intervals were not captured. The partial CPU inference occurred during the incident while P2 was running; P2 host wall/dispatch timing is potentially contaminated, with impact left for root adjudication.

corrected_root_validation.evidence: Root reports group8 command with --validate-only appended, timeout60, return code0, elapsed0.0832s. This is separate from the mistaken attempts and validates fixture structure only.

residual_process_check.method: Read-only scan of /proc cmdline/status at audit time for precision_repro_hf.py and run_expanded_after_predecessors.py; no ps/device query used for this final check.

logs: The wrapper captured stdout/stderr into pipes and did not write a log file. Attempt A/B wrappers had not returned; attempt C wrapper was interrupted. The partial JSON above is the only saved execution artifact located.
limitations: The output file timestamp is a filesystem observation; it is not sufficient to attribute earlier overwritten content to a specific attempt.
No model-load completion or free-run generation is claimed for A/C.
Attempt B proves CPU BF16 reference inference and teacher forcing concurrent with P2; it has no score/adjudication value.

Attempt B has conflicting start observations: ps lstart 06:51:41Z versus /proc stat+btime 06:50:32.140Z, about69s apart. Root-provided /proc timing supports a 527.693s elapsed lower bound to its stop time; exact duration is unresolved.

The saved partial report is proven to be from CPU BF16 inference during the incident, but its attribution between overlapping A/B attempts is uncertain because both wrote to the same path and no prior file hash was recorded.
